exhibits.title: The Cathedral of Descent and Return
exhibits.text:
A cathedral shaped like the letter U: you may only reach the far door by walking DOWN into the crypt and climbing back UP the other side. This is the U-Net, the network that learned to denoise images. The math does not change from the scalar chambers: x_t = √ᾱₜ·x₀ + √(1−ᾱₜ)·ε runs element-wise; ε is now a full field of noise, one N(0,1) draw per pixel; ᾱₜ stays one scalar. Only the sorcerer is promoted: the network must take a noisy field (H, W, C) and hand back predicted noise of the EXACT same shape. A per-pixel prophecy that needs the local grain of a texture AND the global architecture of the scene at once. That double demand is the riddle the U answers.

DESCEND the left arm, the ENCODER halves resolution and doubles channels (256→128→64→32): spatial detail traded for semantic depth. Stand in the CRYPT, the bottleneck, smallest and deepest, the widest field of view: it knows WHAT the picture is, having shed much of WHERE. CLIMB the right arm, the DECODER reverses the trade back to 256, so output shape equals input shape. And because a decoder climbing alone would blur, the cathedral is strung with SKIP CONNECTIONS, flying buttresses carrying each encoder landing's crisp high-resolution detail straight across the nave to the decoder landing at the same height. The forest rises from the crypt; the leaf arrives across the skip. Each landing performs a fixed rite, convolution, timestep injection, self-attention where the map is small enough to afford it, cross-attention to the prompt. Study the plinths; together they are the beating heart of Stable Diffusion.

exhibits.title: The Same Spell, a Greater Sorcerer
exhibits.text: A common misreading: that moving from denoising a number to denoising a picture demands new mathematics. It does not. Scalar and image obey the identical equation, x_t = sqrt(a_bar_t) * x_0 + sqrt(1 - a_bar_t) * eps, for the scalar these are single numbers, for the image they are 256x256x3 arrays and the operation runs element-wise. eps grows into a full array of noise (one standard-normal draw per pixel); a_bar_t remains one scalar, the same noise level for all pixels. Only the NETWORK is promoted. A scalar could be denoised by a tiny MLP. An image demands a map from a noisy field (H, W, C) to predicted noise of the same shape (H, W, C), made per pixel yet informed by the whole scene, local texture and global structure at once. 'Same shape in, same shape out, seen at many scales' is not a decorative wish; it is the design specification, and the U-Net is its answer.

exhibits.title: The U-Shape and Its Flying Buttresses
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  I["noisy image H W C  +  t"] --> E1["encoder 256"]
  E1 --> E2["encoder 128"]
  E2 --> E3["encoder 64"]
  E3 --> B["bottleneck 32 - deepest"]
  B --> D3["decoder 64"]
  D3 --> D2["decoder 128"]
  D2 --> D1["decoder 256"]
  D1 --> O["predicted noise H W C"]
  E3 -. skip .-> D3
  E2 -. skip .-> D2
  E1 -. skip .-> D1
exhibits.caption: Down the left arm the encoder shrinks space and grows channels (256->128->64->32); the bottleneck holds maximum context; up the right arm the decoder grows space back (32->...->256). The dotted skips carry each level's high-resolution detail across to its mirror level. The two arms are symmetric, which is exactly why output shape equals input shape.

exhibits.title: Cross-Section of the Cathedral
exhibits.caption: The cathedral drawn in cross-section. Read it as a building: each block's HEIGHT encodes spatial resolution, its WIDTH the channel count. Descend the left arm and every landing halves the map (256->128->64) while doubling channels, space traded for meaning, until the crypt at 32x32x512 holds the widest field of view and the deepest understanding. Climb the right arm and the trade reverses, resolution doubling back to 256 so the predicted-noise field matches the input shape exactly. The luminous arcs are the flying-buttress SKIP connections: each encoder landing hands its high-resolution detail straight across the nave to the decoder landing of matching size, so the decoder fuses global meaning risen from the crypt with crisp local detail thrown across. Note where the rites sit: convolution does the cheap local work at every level, but self-attention and cross-attention (cost O(n^2)) are afforded only in the shrunken lower rooms near the crypt.

exhibits.title: The Buttresses, What Against Where
exhibits.text: Downsampling is a bargain with a hidden cost. As the encoder shrinks 256 -> 128 -> 64 -> 32, it distils WHAT is in the image, a dog, a skateboard, a sky, but it quietly discards WHERE precisely each edge lay. Rise from the crypt with only that distilled meaning and the decoder must guess the fine positions; its output comes out soft and blurred. The skip connections are the remedy: each encoder level passes its feature map DIRECTLY, at full local resolution, to the decoder level of matching size (64 to 64, 128 to 128, 256 to 256). The decoder then combines global understanding risen from below with sharp detail handed across the skip. This is the same information-highway idea as ResNet's residual connections met in the Attention wing. A path that lets untouched detail flow straight through. Remove the skips and the U-Net still knows what it is drawing; it simply can no longer say exactly where. The difference between them is the difference between a crisp image and a blur.

exhibits.title: Inside a Landing, Conv, Time, and the Familiar Gaze
exhibits.text: Every landing performs three rites. FIRST, a ResNet convolution reads LOCAL features, edges, textures, cheaply, at all resolutions; this is the workhorse. SECOND, the timestep t is injected. The block must know WHICH noise level it is undoing, so t is turned into a vector by a sinusoidal embedding, the very positional-encoding trick from the basement's Wheel of Frequencies, and added into the features. THIRD, and only where the map is small, SELF-ATTENTION. This is EXACTLY the (n, n) attention from the Attention wing, now over spatial positions: flatten a 32x32xC feature map into a sequence of n = 1024 positions of dimension C, and let every position attend to every other. The score matrix is (1024, 1024), a million entries, each pixel-position weighing every other. Crucially, attention only MIXES; it never changes shape. Flatten (32,32,C) -> (1024,C) is lossless rearrangement; (1024,1024) @ (1024,C) = (1024,C), same count, same dimension; reshape back to (32,32,C) is pure bookkeeping. The big score matrix is a consumed intermediate that never appears in the input or output shape. Why only at low resolution? Cost is O(n^2). At 32x32, n=1024 gives a tidy ~1M-entry matrix. At 256x256, n=65,536 gives roughly 4 BILLION entries, ruinous. So convolution does the cheap local work at high resolution, and attention is reserved for the crypt-near levels where global reasoning is affordable.

exhibits.title: The Second Gaze, Listening to the Prompt
exhibits.text: A denoiser that only looked at itself could make a coherent picture of ANYTHING. To make the picture the one you ASKED for, a fourth rite is inserted right after self-attention: CROSS-ATTENTION between image and text. The prompt 'a corgi on a skateboard' is first turned into vectors by a text encoder (CLIP or T5), say shape (7, 768), computed once and reused at every diffusion step and every U-Net level. Then the wiring, identical to the chamber of The Two Gazes: Q comes from the IMAGE positions (1024, d); K and V come from the TEXT tokens (7, d). The score Q.K^T is (1024, 7), NOT square, because the two sides have different lengths, and the output (1024, 7) @ (7, d) = (1024, d) returns to image shape. Each image position asks 'which words are relevant to me?': skateboard-region patches attend to the token 'skateboard', dog-region patches to 'corgi'. This is the same image-into-text cross-attention you met in the Attention wing; here it is the steering wheel. Self-attention buys internal coherence; cross-attention buys agreement with the prompt. The two gazes together are what make text-to-image diffusion obey your words.

exhibits.title: The Four Rites of a Landing, in Order
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  A["ResNet conv - local features"] --> B["inject timestep t - which noise level"]
  B --> C["self-attention - image to image - coherence"]
  C --> D["cross-attention - image to text - prompt steering"]
  D --> O["out - same shape as in"]
exhibits.caption: The full block, in fixed order: convolution for local features, timestep injection so the block knows the noise level, self-attention for spatial coherence (image looking at itself), then cross-attention for prompt steering (image listening to the text tokens). This four-step landing, stacked down and up the U, is the core of Stable Diffusion.
